definitions.explanation: An unpleasant bitter or sharp taste, often associated with raw vegetables like bamboo shoots, spinach, or eggplant. Removed by blanching, soaking, or other preparation.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦ほうれん{草|そう}→ほうれん草：05188_hourensou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧えぐみ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{強|つよ}い→強い：00820_tsuyoi⟧。
examples.english: This spinach has a strong acrid taste.

examples.japanese: ⟦{湯|ゆ}→湯：01740_yu⟧でること⟦で→で：00502_de⟧えぐみ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{抜|ぬ}ける→抜ける：02385_nukeru⟧。
examples.english: The astringency goes away when you boil it.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}いタケノコ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧えぐみ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{少|すく}なくて→少ない：01136_sukunai⟧⟦{食|た}べやすい→食べやすい：21799_tabeyasui⟧。
examples.english: Young bamboo shoots have less astringency and are easier to eat.

notes:
The noun form of the adjective ⟦えぐい→えぐい：05608_egui⟧ (acrid, harsh). Refers to a specific unpleasant taste caused by oxalic acid, alkaloids, or similar compounds in raw plant matter.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- えぐみ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{強|つよ}い→強い：00820_tsuyoi⟧: to have strong astringency
- えぐみ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{抜|ぬ}く→抜く：02384_nuku⟧: to remove the astringency (by soaking, blanching, etc.)
- えぐみ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{気|き}になる→気になる：03027_kininaru⟧: the astringency is noticeable/bothersome
- えぐみ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦{野菜|やさい}→野菜：02265_yasai⟧: vegetables with astringency

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {苦|にが}み: bitterness — broader; includes pleasant bitterness like in coffee
- ⟦{渋|しぶ}み→渋み：07149_shibumi⟧: astringent flavor — the pucker-inducing taste of strong tea, persimmons
- アク: scum, harshness — overlaps with えぐみ; refers to both the foam from boiling and the underlying harsh taste
